derivation_notes: For a two-state nonpermissive-permissive gate at equilibrium, the ratio of state probabilities follows a Boltzmann factor whose free-energy difference varies linearly with voltage. Normalizing the two state probabilities gives this bounded sigmoid; slope_factor > 0 ensures that activation is nondecreasing with depolarization.

scenario_text: A voltage-clamp experiment samples membrane potential while temperature and ionic conditions remain fixed. The target is the steady fraction of activation gates occupying the permissive conformation in a voltage-sensitive neuronal ion channel. Voltage-dependent changes in conformational occupancy produce a bounded sigmoidal response. Transient gating and channel inactivation are excluded from the baseline question.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.asymmetry_factor: small signed values such that 1 + asymmetry_factor*(V - V_half) stays positive over the sampled voltage range; often Abs(asymmetry_factor)*(max Abs(V - V_half)) < 1

derivation_notes: The parent assumes one voltage-independent effective gating sensitivity for the whole activation transition. Here the apparent slope scale is allowed to vary linearly with voltage around V_half, representing redistribution among nearby substates that changes effective gating charge while preserving a static bounded steady-state mapping.
change_summary: The constant slope_factor was replaced by a voltage-dependent effective slope_factor*(1 + asymmetry_factor*(V - V_half)). This creates an asymmetric monotone activation curve with different lower- and upper-flank curvature under the same voltage-clamp conditions.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Activation is represented by one effective gating transition with a voltage-independent slope_factor.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Voltage-dependent redistribution among closely related permissive and nonpermissive substates makes the apparent gating charge vary with voltage, altering steady-state curvature without adding dynamics.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when asymmetry_factor = 0, making the effective slope constant and equal to slope_factor.

response_change.parent_relation: The steady activation curve is a single symmetric Boltzmann sigmoid of V with one shared slope_factor, so semilogistic steepness is fixed across the whole transition.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single effective voltage sensitivity by a voltage-dependent effective slope/charge, yielding an asymmetric but still monotone bounded activation curve whose local steepness differs below versus above V_half.
response_change.observable_effect: Across a voltage-clamp activation curve spanning both subthreshold and suprathreshold voltages, the child can show a broader foot with a sharper mid-to-upper activation rise, or the converse, while remaining bounded between 0 and 1; one parent sigmoid with one refitted slope_factor cannot match both flanks simultaneously.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when sampled voltages cover a substantial portion of both sides of the transition, roughly |V - V_half| on the order of slope_factor to a few slope_factor, so flank asymmetry or changing local steepness is resolvable; with only a narrow window near midpoint the refinement may be weakly identifiable.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, differing lower- and upper-flank steepness is already visible within the sampled activation range; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to more pronounced tail-versus-midrange curvature differences without changing the bounded monotone character.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered when the voltage dependence of the effective slope collapses to a constant, so the asymmetric sigmoid reduces to the original single Boltzmann form.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Voltage-dependent redistribution among closely related permissive and nonpermissive substates can make the apparent gating charge vary with voltage, producing asymmetric steady-state activation without introducing time dependence or inactivation.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient of the existing Boltzmann exponent denominator now depends on V itself, changing local curvature across the sampled activation range instead of globally rescaling steepness.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Activation is represented by one effective gating transition with a voltage-independent slope_factor.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective voltage-sensitivity scale varies with voltage around V_half due to substate redistribution, making the steady activation curve asymmetric while remaining bounded and monotone over admissible ranges.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting asymmetry_factor = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: with temperature and ionic conditions fixed, varying only clamped voltage V maps to m_inf through one symmetric Boltzmann curve centered at V_half and scaled by one constant slope_factor. Child change: the effective slope is larger on one side of V_half and smaller on the other, so the target mapping itself shows unequal lower- and upper-flank steepness while staying between 0 and 1. This is observable when voltages span both subthreshold and suprathreshold activation, roughly from near-zero to near-saturating m_inf, where flank asymmetry can be resolved.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast across those conditions because refitting V_half only translates the sigmoid and refitting slope_factor rescales steepness globally and symmetrically. The child changes the scored mapping from V to m_inf by introducing flank-specific curvature, not merely auxiliary behavior, so one shared symmetric parent curve cannot match both foot and upper-rise steepness simultaneously over the same voltage range.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one constant effective gating charge or voltage-sensitivity scale for the entire activation transition, forcing a symmetric logistic shape that cannot represent asymmetric steady-state activation curves seen when conformational energy landscapes are not perfectly two-state.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Activation is represented by one effective gating transition with a voltage-independent slope_factor.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Voltage-dependent redistribution among closely related permissive and nonpermissive substates can make the apparent gating charge vary with voltage, producing asymmetric steady-state activation without introducing time dependence or inactivation.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with temperature and ionic conditions fixed, varying only clamped voltage V maps to m_inf through one symmetric Boltzmann curve centered at V_half and scaled by one constant slope_factor. Scientific gap: real steady activation can remain monotone and bounded yet show unequal lower- and upper-flank steepness because the effective voltage sensitivity changes across the transition. Child contrast: under the same fixed environment and still at steady state, the activation foot can be shallower while the upper rise is steeper, or vice versa, changing the target mapping itself rather than only an auxiliary trajectory. This is observable when the protocol samples voltages well below and above V_half over an activation range from near 0 toward near 1. A single parent parameter set cannot absorb that contrast across those conditions because refitting V_half shifts the curve and refitting slope_factor rescales steepness globally, but neither creates flank-specific curvature asymmetry. Limitation: if measurements cover only a narrow central voltage band or remain far from saturation, the added asymmetry may not be distinguishable.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.V_half: sampled across condition-specific midpoint shifts that keep the activation transition within the measured voltage window; e.g. several millivolts around a nominal midpoint while preserving 1 + asymmetry_factor*(V - V_half) > 0 over sampled V

derivation_notes: The scientific refinement promotes V_half from a fixed parameter to an independently sampled input representing ionic-condition-dependent shifts in the free-energy balance between permissive and nonpermissive conformations. The algebraic law is therefore interpreted as a threshold surface m_inf(V, V_half) rather than a single shared activation curve m_inf(V).
change_summary: Relaxed the fixed-environment assumption by allowing ionic conditions to shift the activation midpoint, implemented by promoting V_half to an input. This changes the scored mapping from one voltage-only sigmoid to a bounded monotone surface over voltage and ionic condition.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The half-activation voltage V_half is constant because ionic conditions are fixed across all observations.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Steady electrostatic screening or ionic binding can shift the voltage where permissive and nonpermissive conformations are equally favorable, moving the activation midpoint between sampled ionic environments.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: At any fixed ionic condition, V_half takes one constant value and the model reduces to the parent single-curve law for that condition; in particular, when the promoted midpoint is held fixed at the dataset's original constant value, the parent expression is exactly recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed ionic conditions, m_inf is a one-input sigmoidal function of V with a single shared half-activation location V_half and voltage-dependent asymmetry around that location.
response_change.child_relation: Release the fixed-environment assumption by allowing the activation curve's midpoint to depend on one additional sampled ionic-condition input, so m_inf becomes a bounded monotone surface over voltage and that condition rather than a single voltage-only curve.
response_change.observable_effect: Across recordings taken at different fixed ionic conditions, the voltage giving half-activation shifts systematically while the low- and high-voltage saturations remain bounded; a single parent curve with one shared parameter set cannot align both conditions when plotted against the same V axis.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the experiment includes at least two fixed ionic-condition settings that measurably alter electrostatic stabilization of permissive versus nonpermissive conformations, while asymmetry_factor remains small enough that the denominator stays positive over the sampled voltage range.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, differing ionic settings produce parallel or near-parallel displaced activation curves; in holdout, intermediate or more extreme settings continue the same midpoint-shift trend, extending the threshold surface beyond the training voltages.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the added ionic-condition dependence vanishes, so the midpoint becomes constant and equal to the original V_half for all conditions.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: With voltage as the only sampled input, the parent can represent only one activation curve. A condition-dependent shift in conformational free-energy bias requires the midpoint itself to vary across sampled environments; refitting separate fixed V_half values per condition would not be a single shared mapping.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Steady electrostatic screening or ionic binding effects can shift the voltage at which the two conformational occupancies are equally favorable, moving the activation midpoint without requiring inactivation or time dependence.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored mapping now depends jointly on two sampled quantities through the displacement V - V_half, creating a threshold surface across environments rather than one globally shared curve.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: V_half is invariant across all sampled observations because ionic conditions are fixed.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: V_half varies across sampled ionic conditions and acts as an independently sampled midpoint input in the steady-state activation law.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Holding V_half fixed across all observations recovers the parent single-input law exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: with ionic conditions fixed, m_inf follows one sigmoidal curve of V centered at a single shared V_half, with asymmetry only through the voltage-dependent denominator. Child change: when ionic conditions vary between recordings and are encoded through sampled V_half, the midpoint shifts so the scored target becomes m_inf(V, V_half), a bounded monotone threshold surface rather than one universal curve. This is observable by comparing steady-state activation at at least two ionic settings while holding temperature fixed: the voltage where m_inf is near 0.5 moves systematically with condition, provided the shift remains within the sampled activation range and 1 + asymmetry_factor*(V - V_half) stays positive.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce multiple condition-specific half-activation voltages across those ionic settings because its midpoint is structurally fixed for all observations. Retuning slope_factor or asymmetry_factor only changes steepness or skew around one shared center and cannot place distinct 0.5 crossings at different voltages on the same common V axis; separate per-condition refits would no longer be one shared mapping.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: With voltage as the only sampled input, the parent can represent only one activation curve. A condition-dependent shift in conformational free-energy bias requires the midpoint itself to vary across sampled environments; refitting separate fixed V_half values per condition would not be a single shared mapping.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model treats the half-activation voltage as invariant even though changes in ionic environment can shift the electrostatic free-energy difference between permissive and nonpermissive conformations at steady state.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that ionic conditions are fixed, specifically the implied constancy of V_half across all sampled observations.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Steady electrostatic screening or ionic binding effects can shift the voltage at which the two conformational occupancies are equally favorable, moving the activation midpoint without requiring inactivation or time dependence.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: for all observations, m_inf is determined solely by V through one sigmoidal curve centered at a single constant V_half, with slope variation handled only by the voltage-dependent denominator. Changed mapping: if ionic conditions are allowed to vary between observations, the free-energy balance underlying half-activation can shift, so the target becomes a surface in which the threshold depends on both V and the sampled condition encoded through promoted V_half. Distinguishing condition: vary ionic conditions between voltage-clamp protocols while holding temperature fixed and still measuring steady-state activation; then compare the voltages where m_inf is about 0.5. The child predicts those voltages move systematically with condition, whereas the parent with one shared parameter set can only place one midpoint and therefore cannot match multiple condition-specific half-activation locations simultaneously. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary effect, because the scored steady-state m_inf(V, condition) itself changes. Admissible regime: the shift should be large enough to be resolved over the sampled voltage window but not so large that activation leaves the observable transition range; asymmetry_factor should remain in the stated small range so monotonicity and boundedness are preserved. Limitation: if ionic conditions truly remain fixed in all data, this refinement will not activate and should not be claimed as additional observable complexity.
